channelTitle: The inventor who asked for rice and nearly bankrupted an empire
hook: A wise man asked an emperor for 'just some rice' - and the math ruined the palace treasury.
storyParts: Legend says the inventor of chess showed his game to an emperor, who offered any reward. The inventor asked only for rice: one grain on the first square, doubled each square after.
The emperor laughed and agreed - until his treasurers did the math. By the 64th square the pile needed was bigger than every harvest in the empire combined, many times over.
Some versions say the inventor was made chief advisor for outsmarting the court. Others say he was executed for embarrassing the emperor. Either way, nobody forgot the lesson.
moral: Grandma June's takeaway: never laugh at a small number that's doubling - it's how most fortunes and most debts are really made.
cta: Would you have taken the rice deal? Tell Grandma June what you'd have asked for instead
